lead.headline: Big Stric played the early window a man down
lead.dek: Dalton Kincaid never played, and Big Stric Energy’s tight end slot went into the books at 0.0. The champ leads 116.42 to 88.22 and is 83.2% to win the game that decides who stays alive.
lead.pull: You can survive a bad game from your quarterback. Surviving a position that doesn’t exist is harder.
body: 1:49 PM, and it’s official. Big Stric Energy started Dalton Kincaid, Kincaid was Out with the thumb, and Big Stric’s tight end slot is a final 0.0. Tucker Kraft was on bye. The bench never had a tight end. Both of this morning’s wire answers, Darren Waller and Dawson Knox, have already played. That spot is closed for the week. That’s a busted lineup in the biggest game this franchise has left.

And it stings worse because of who’s across the field. The champ, Maye I touch your TDs?, is starting Michael Mayer at tight end, the most-added player in football this week. Mayer is playing right now. Big Stric’s guy is in street clothes.

The rest of the early window didn’t bail it out. Josh Allen finished with 14.16 against a 24.67 projection. Tyler Bass kicked in 17.0, Nico Collins 14.8, Rashee Rice 11.3. Saquon Barkley put up 13.5 on the bench while Braelon Allen sits at 2.6 in the lineup. Meanwhile the champ cashed Emmett Johnson (24.3), Cam Ward (22.22) and Bucky Irving (19.0). Scoreboard: 116.42 to 88.22.

It isn’t over. Big Stric has 5 players left: Justin Jefferson hasn’t kicked off, and Geno Smith, Braelon Allen, Ashton Jeanty and the Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST are on the field. The champ also has 5 left, starting with Brock Purdy. The live projection says 168.32 to 144.65. Big Stric needs 23.67 points it isn’t projected to find, and Jefferson is the only player big enough to find them.

My read: 16.8% sounds about right. The zero at tight end didn’t lose this game by itself. It just made sure the margin for everything else was gone before lunch. If Big Stric loses this one, this is the slot everyone will point to.

quick_hits.headline: Poochinski hung 175.04 on the early window
quick_hits.body: Poochinski made its calls this morning and then the lineup went off: Dak Prescott 35.9, CeeDee Lamb 30.2, Jahmyr Gibbs 27.8, Javonte Williams 24.1. It leads Santa Clara’s Finest 175.04 to 55.86 and is 98% to win with Chase Brown and the San Francisco 49ers D/ST still to go. The first call of the morning, Luther Burden III, gave it 3.3. Nobody will remember.

quick_hits.headline: Santa Clara’s Finest has 6 left and a 2% shot
quick_hits.body: Santa Clara’s Finest hold the last playoff spot at 57.1%, but this week is slipping: 6 players left, including Joe Burrow (26.4) and Stefon Diggs (13.41), and a 148.65 live projection against 197.67. With the champ 83.2% to win its own game, the race for that last spot is about to tighten.

quick_hits.headline: Cherry Blossom trails by a lot and is 74.1% anyway
quick_hits.body: Bad things man bad things posted 136.16 in the early window, with Chuba Hubbard at 26.0 and C.J. Stroud at 21.46. It has 2 left: Kirk Cousins and Evan McPherson. Cherry Blossom has 91.58 and 5 left, including Christian McCaffrey (19.95) and Tee Higgins (18.91), and projects 175.98 to 160.37. Travis Kelce’s 25.4 is why the math still works.

quick_hits.headline: Four lineup calls, four answers
quick_hits.body: deeboliciouskins added Drew Stevens for Jason Myers at 9:42 AM. Cherry Blossom went Jonah Coleman over Brock Bowers. Poochinski slotted Burden for Jadarian Price and added the 49ers D/ST at 12:51 PM. The champ kept Matt Gay, and Gay is kicking right now.
